title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated connectors can create, update and delete in third-party systems
summary: Hold: the briefing says admin-published federated connectors are read-only, but Microsoft's dedicated documentation says they can also create, update and delete data where supported. The roadmap details, licensing and five administrative paths are supported; the briefing should also acknowledge conflicting overview documentation and its missing audit-control row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Publisher-provided create, update and delete tools let users modify third-party records without leaving Copilot.
claims.quote: When a connector provides the appropriate tools, users can ask Microsoft 365 Copilot to create, update, or delete information in a connected third-party system on their behalf. Users can complete work without leaving Copilot.
claims.fix: Add: 'The general Copilot connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, while the dedicated federated connectors overview documents write actions.' The conflicting page is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to query external systems in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: No data is indexed into Microsoft 365. Copilot sends the connector the information it needs to complete the action and returns the outcome to the user.

claims.claim: Federated connectors were read-only before the October 2026 write-action change.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: Actions use the user's account and source-system permissions and cannot make changes the user could not make directly.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.where: What's changing: The roadmap item says every
claims.claim: The roadmap says every create, update or delete action requires explicit user confirmation.
claims.quote: every create, update, or delete action requires the user's explicit confirmation before it runs.

claims.where: What's changing: The roadmap item says administrators
claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can view read and write/delete tools in the admin center and disable connectors.
claims.quote: Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to Needs approval, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: confirmation card
claims.claim: The confirmation card lets users inspect the action parameters before approving.
claims.quote: Users can expand the card to review the action parameters before approving it.

claims.claim: While an action awaits confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.
claims.quote: While an action is awaiting confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow once; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Allow once approves the current action and asks again on the next use of the tool.
claims.quote: Allow once | Runs the action now. Copilot asks again the next time it wants to use the tool.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses further confirmation for that tool during the current conversation.
claims.quote: Allow for conversation | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.where: What's changing: Always allow; Risk assessment: indefinitely
claims.claim: Always allow creates a reusable approval without a time-based expiry, subject to user revocation and publisher changes.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Cancel; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cancel declines the action and leaves the connected system unchanged.
claims.quote: Cancel | Declines the action. Nothing is changed in the connected system.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls: reusable approvals
claims.claim: Reusable approvals apply to individual tools rather than the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.where: What's changing: revocable; Governance controls: Users manage individual tool approvals
claims.claim: Users review or reset approval settings under Settings > Sources > connector > Tools > Write/Delete tools.
claims.quote: Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot by going to Settings > Sources and selecting the connector. The Tools section groups the connector's Write/Delete tools separately from its Read tools.

claims.where: What's changing: publisher adds or changes
claims.claim: A new or changed write-capable tool defaults back to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.quote: Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.claim: On supported connectors, admins sign in in the connector's Tools section and select All tools to inspect modifying tools.
claims.quote:
On the connector's details page, go to the Tools section and sign in to the third-party service.

Select All tools, and then review the list to identify tools that can create, update, or delete data.

claims.claim: The admin tool list reflects the permissions of the account used to sign in.
claims.quote: The tool list reflects the permissions of the account used to sign in.

claims.claim: Learn directs users to Settings > Sources > connector > Write/Delete tools when the admin tool view is unavailable.
claims.quote: If you encounter issues, sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot with your user account, go to Settings -> Sources, and select the connector. Then expand Write/Delete tools.

claims.claim: Supported write-capable experiences include Copilot Chat, agents, Cowork and Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
- Agents
- Cowork
- Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
- Researcher agent

The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions.

claims.claim: Researcher remains read-only.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft-provided default federated connectors appear as Ready in the admin-center connections list.
claims.quote: Default federated connectors are provided by Microsoft and appear as Ready in your connections list in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing: admin-published; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Admin-published connector templates currently support read-only tools and write support is still a future question.
claims.quote: Admin-published FCCs can also create, update, or delete data where the connector provides those tools, with the user's approval and subject to their permissions in the source system. Supported actions vary by connector.
claims.fix: Replace the read-only statements in What's changing and Scope with: 'Admin-published federated connectors can also create, update or delete data where the connector provides those tools, with user approval and subject to source-system permissions; supported actions vary by connector.' In Governance guidance, remove 'and for admin-published connectors gaining write support'. Remove the open question asking when admin-published connectors will support write tools. Keep the existing citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/admin-published-federated-connectors.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The write capability arrives on existing enabled connectors without a separate administrator enablement step.
claims.quote:
Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Write actions export Customer Data from the Copilot interaction to the connected third-party system.
claims.quote: These actions export Customer Data to the connected system to create, update, delete, or otherwise modify data.

claims.claim: Federated connector access uses the user's OAuth connection.
claims.quote: Secure by design; federated access respects source permissions and authentication (OAuth 2.0).

claims.where: Risk assessment: static egress IP ranges
claims.claim: An MCP server restricting inbound source IPs must allow Microsoft's static egress IP addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Copilot selects tools dynamically
claims.claim: Copilot dynamically selects relevant tools at runtime.
claims.quote: When appropriate, Microsoft 365 Copilot dynamically selects relevant tools to retrieve information or perform an action.

claims.where: Risk assessment: No administrator override; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant-wide administrator override forcing Needs approval is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors write tools admin enforce approval always allow tenant Purview audit approval static egress IP; "federated connectors" "always" "administrator" "approval". Read federated-connectors-overview, manage-federated-connectors and Agent 365 MCP tool controls.

claims.claim: Every querying user needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote:
A Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license for every user who queries the federated source.

Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.quote: Packaging a capability doesn't remove the cost of operating its dependencies. Include hosting, model usage, storage, networking, credentials, monitoring, and support for any remote MCP servers, APIs, or other services your plugin uses.
